fact_text: For a third-country national, the temporary residence and work permit (the 'single permit') is one document that combines a residence permit and a work permit, so a separately issued work permit is not additionally required.
evidence_quote: The temporary residence and work permit is called a "single permit", because combines elements of:

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a foreigner must obtain two separate documents in Poland (a residence permit and a work permit). Actually the single permit is one card that legalises both stay and work at once. Action: apply for the temporary residence and work permit instead of a stand-alone work permit.

fact_text: The single permit is not renewed automatically; before it expires the foreigner must file a fresh application for a residence permit to keep their stay legal.
evidence_quote: Permit is not renewed automatically. The foreigner who wishes to continue staying in Poland should, before its expiry, apply for a residence permit

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the permit rolls over or that the employer's HR handles renewal automatically. Actually it lapses unless the foreigner personally reapplies before expiry. Action: diary the permit expiry date and submit the next application ahead of it.

fact_text: The single-permit application cannot be lodged from abroad; it must be submitted while the foreigner is physically present in Poland during a legal stay.
evidence_quote: The application must be submitted during your stay in Poland.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a relocating employee can file the Polish residence application from the home country before arriving. Actually filing from abroad via the MOS system is not permitted. Action: enter Poland on the correct visa first, then apply while legally present.

fact_text: The residence-permit application must be signed personally by the foreigner; it cannot be signed by a representative or by the employer.
evidence_quote: Therefore, the application cannot be signed by a representative or the foreigner’s employer.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the employer or an immigration agent can sign and submit the whole residence application on the employee's behalf. Actually the Act on Foreigners requires the foreigner's own signature for the application to be processed. Action: ensure the employee personally signs (e-signs via login.gov.pl).

fact_text: Any document in a foreign language filed for the residence permit must be accompanied by a sworn (certified) translation into Polish.
evidence_quote: Documents in a foreign language must be presented together with a sworn translation into Polish.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed English-language supporting documents are accepted as-is for the permit file. Actually each foreign-language document needs a sworn Polish translation. Action: budget time and cost for a sworn translator (register kept by the Ministry of Justice).

fact_text: A third-country national's authorisation to work can come from a work permit obtained for them by their employer, or from a single (temporary residence and work) permit they obtain themselves.
evidence_quote: this authorization may stem either from a document permitting them to work in Poland, which was obtained for them by their employer (e.g., a work permit)

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the worker always applies for their own Polish work authorisation. Actually a stand-alone work permit is applied for by the employer (to the voivode), whereas the single permit is applied for by the worker. Action: confirm with the employer which route they are using before signing a contract.

fact_text: Holding a Polish visa or residence permit does not by itself allow a foreigner to work; the specific visa or permit type must permit employment.
evidence_quote: make sure that the foreigner’s visa or residence permit allows them to work in Poland—not every visa and not every temporary residence permit permits this.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed any valid Polish visa or residence card lets you take a job. Actually only visas/permits issued for a work-eligible purpose do, so some statuses bar employment even with a work permit. Action: verify the visa/permit purpose code permits work before starting.

fact_text: Poland's EU Blue Card is a single permit for highly-qualified work that also grants EU-wide advantages, including easier movement within the EU and faster acquisition of EU long-term resident status.
evidence_quote: the possibility of easier movement within the EU and faster acquisition of EU long-term resident status.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the Blue Card is just another Polish work permit. Actually it is part of the EU Blue Card system, giving easier intra-EU mobility and a faster path to EU long-term resident status. Action: for a qualifying senior/specialist role, consider the Blue Card over the ordinary single permit.

fact_text: The Blue Card / high-qualification permit is granted for the period of work plus three extra months, ranging from more than 6 months up to 3 years.
evidence_quote: a period 3 months longer than the period of performing work - from more than 6 months to 3 years.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the permit matches exactly the employment-contract dates. Actually it is granted for the work period plus a three-month buffer (min. just over 6 months, max 3 years). Action: expect a short grace buffer, but still reapply before expiry rather than relying on it.

fact_text: Proof of health insurance is a mandatory condition for granting the residence-and-work / Blue Card permit to a third-country national.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed health cover is only sorted out after arrival through payroll. Actually the foreigner must already have health insurance for the permit to be granted. Action: line up qualifying health insurance (e.g. via ZUS/NFZ registration on the employment, or private cover) as part of the permit file.

fact_text: After a permit is granted, a third-country national receives a residence card (karta pobytu); it confirms their identity and, with a valid travel document, allows multiple crossings of the Polish border without a visa.
evidence_quote: allows for multiple crossings of the Polish border without the need to obtain a visa or meet the entry requirements for visa-free travel, upon presentation of a valid travel document;

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a new visa is needed each time to re-enter Poland after travelling. Actually the residence card plus a valid passport lets the holder re-cross the Polish border without a visa. Action: always travel with both the karta pobytu and a valid passport.

fact_text: The first residence card is in most cases issued automatically (ex officio) after the permit decision becomes final, without the foreigner filing a separate application for the card itself.
evidence_quote: First residence card is in most cases issued ex officio, therefore without the necessity of submitting an application for its issuance.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you must lodge a second, separate application for the physical residence card. Actually the first card is normally issued ex officio once the permit is final and the fee is paid. Action: pay the card fee and wait for the collection notice rather than filing a new application.

fact_text: A third-country driving licence that does not conform to the Geneva or Vienna Convention model can only be exchanged for a Polish licence after passing the theoretical part of the state driving exam.
evidence_quote: Jeżeli twoje prawo jazdy nie jest zgodne ze wzorem określonym w Konwencji Genewskiej lub Konwencji Wiedeńskiej – musisz zdać część teoretyczną egzaminu państwowego.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed any foreign licence can simply be swapped for a Polish one. Actually EU/EFTA/Swiss licences are exempt from exchange, and a non-Convention third-country licence requires passing the Polish theory exam first. Action: check whether the issuing country follows the Geneva/Vienna Convention model; if not, plan for the theory exam.
